## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Why

`HuggingFaceTokenizer.apply_chat_template` rendered with `messages` and the caller's kwargs only. Jinja's default Undefined becomes an empty string, so a template that prints `{{ bos_token }}` or `{{ eos_token }}` dropped both. Default recipes use `HuggingFaceTokenizer`, not the experiment subclass that already passed those strings.

`encode(..., add_bos=True)` only prepends BOS. It does not put EOS between turns. `ChatProcessor` calls `encode` that way on the rendered string, then appends one EOS if the last id is not already EOS.

**Example.** Asset template in `tests/assets/tokenizer` (`bos_token` is `<|begin_of_text|>`, `eos_token` is `<|end_of_text|>`), messages `user/hi` then `assistant/yo`:

```text
before: user\nhiassistant\nyo
after:  <|begin_of_text|>user\nhi<|end_of_text|>assistant\nyo<|end_of_text|>
```

Same text, `encode(..., add_bos=True, add_eos=False)` on that asset tokenizer:

```text
before: [2002, 117, 115, 101, 114, 104, 105, 97, 115, 115, 105, 115, 116, 97, 110, 116, 121, 111]
        one BOS (2002) prepended; no EOS id
after:  [2002, 117, 115, 101, 114, 104, 105, 2003, 97, 115, 115, 105, 115, 116, 97, 110, 116, 121, 111, 2003]
        BOS once; EOS (2003) after each turn
```

## What changed

- `HuggingFaceTokenizer.apply_chat_template` passes `bos_token` and `eos_token` via `setdefault`. Caller kwargs win. A missing token is `""`, so Jinja does not see Undefined.
- `HuggingFaceTokenizer.encode` sets `add_bos=False` when the text already starts with `bos_token`, so `ChatProcessor`'s `add_bos=True` does not insert a second BOS.
- `HFBackendTokenizer.apply_chat_template` and `encode` are deleted. They repeated the base `setdefault` and the BOS prefix check. `__init__` still repairs eos when `eos_id` was left unset, and `set_chat_template` still rewrites `{% generation %}` tags.
- `encode`'s `add_bos` docstring says the prepend is skipped when the text already starts with `bos_token`.
- `DefaultRenderer`'s error no longer names `bos_token` as a variable this tokenizer omits. It names the rest of the special-token map (`pad_token`, `unk_token`, ...).
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_chat_dataset.py` still expects the corrected render. `TestHuggingFaceTokenizerChatTemplateTokens` is gone (`test_shifted_by_one` already checks that string and one BOS id). `TestHFBackendTokenizerChatLabels` is `TestChatTemplateSpecialTokens` on `HuggingFaceTokenizer` and still checks answer-only labels.

## Alternatives considered

- Point every recipe at `HFBackendTokenizer`. That subclass also rewrites `{% generation %}` tags and repairs eos when bos and eos are the same string. Default SFT should not depend on the experiment tokenizer for variables the base tokenizer already knows.
- Leave the two overrides on `HFBackendTokenizer`. No. After the base change they only ran the same `setdefault` and prefix check a second time.
- Inject the strings in `BaseTokenizer.apply_chat_template`. The base class has no `bos_token` or `eos_token`.
- Splice BOS/EOS inside `ChatProcessor` after rendering. The template already says where they go, and any other `apply_chat_template` caller would still drop them.

## User-facing changes

This changes SFT chat strings for every recipe that uses `HuggingFaceTokenizer` and a template that references `bos_token` / `eos_token`. Templates that do not reference those names are unchanged, because the extra kwargs are unused. `encode` changes only when the text already starts with `bos_token`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `{{ bos_token }}` / `{{ eos_token }}` render as empty strings | They render this tokenizer's BOS and EOS strings (`""` if unset) |
| `encode(rendered, add_bos=True)` prepends BOS even when the template already wrote it | One BOS id |
| EOS shows up only if the caller appends it (ChatProcessor appends one at the end) | EOS is present wherever the template writes `{{ eos_token }}`, including between turns |
| Caller-supplied `bos_token=` / `eos_token=` | Still win |

## Numerics

Not bitwise-identical. Chat token ids change for those templates, so SFT loss on the same rows will not match the base commit `4759738106a6f198a4dd41c78d2a754be5d0b2c4`. No GPU loss comparison. No golden loss files to regenerate: this does not change the model forward, only the chat strings fed to it. Pretraining text that does not start with `bos_token` encodes as before.

## Testing

- The token behavior is the previous commit on this branch. This commit does not change `setdefault` or the prefix check. `py_compile` of the four touched files succeeded. `ufmt` 2.3.0 reported them already formatted.
- `/opt/homebrew/anaconda3/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_chat_dataset.py -q` still does not collect here (`spmd_types` has no `rules`, then NumPy 2.2.6 vs bottleneck). CI has to run it. `{% generation %}` coverage stays in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/test_tokenizer.py`.

## Known issues / follow-ups

Local collection failure above is an environment mismatch, not this diff. No follow-up code change.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The bug is real on `main`: Llama-3-style templates that reference `bos_token`/`eos_token` render without them on the default SFT path. The fix belongs in `HuggingFaceTokenizer`, but it should replace the identical experiment overrides rather than duplicate them. This touches core, so a maintainer still needs to review.

**What this PR does.** It moves two behaviors from the experiment `HFBackendTokenizer` into `HuggingFaceTokenizer`:
- `apply_chat_template` passes `bos_token`/`eos_token` to the Jinja template (caller kwargs still win).
- `encode` skips prepending BOS when the text already starts with the BOS string.

SFT token ids change for templates that reference those variables. That is expected and explained in the description. No golden loss files are affected.

**Example.** Test asset template `{{ bos_token }}{% for m in messages %}{{ m.role }}\n{{ m.content }}{{ eos_token }}{% endfor %}`, messages user/hi, assistant/yo, run through `ChatProcessor`:
```text
main: "user\nhiassistant\nyo"                                   -> [BOS] user\nhi assistant\nyo [EOS appended by ChatProcessor]
PR:   "<|begin_of_text|>user\nhi<|end_of_text|>assistant\nyo<|end_of_text|>" -> [BOS] user\nhi [EOS] assistant\nyo [EOS]
```
The real Llama 3 template writes `{{- bos_token }}` and `<|eot_id|>`. So on `main` only BOS was missing; ChatProcessor's `add_bos=True` was covering for it.

### Must fix
1. The PR description's "Summary (human-written)" section is empty. The author needs to fill it in.
2. `torchtitan/experiments/transformers_modeling_backend/tokenizer.py:46-55`: `HFBackendTokenizer.apply_chat_template` and `.encode` are now exact duplicates of the new base code. Delete them and fix the class docstring (details inline at `tokenizer.py:429`).
3. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_chat_dataset.py:344`: `TestHuggingFaceTokenizerChatTemplateTokens` duplicates `test_shifted_by_one`. Delete it, and switch `TestHFBackendTokenizerChatLabels` to `HuggingFaceTokenizer`.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/components/tokenizer.py:460`: `encode` now overrides an explicit `add_bos=True`. Document that in the `add_bos` docstring.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_chat_dataset.py:200`: four of the five new token assertions are implied by the exact-string check or by the code just above them.
- `torchtitan/components/renderer.py:80-81`: the `DefaultRenderer` error message still names `bos_token` as a missing template variable. Change the example (e.g. "`pad_token`, `unk_token`, ...") or say "HF's full `special_tokens_map`".

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Gate: the problem is concrete (asset template plus Llama 3), the root cause is in the right layer (the tokenizer owns `bos_token`/`eos_token`; `BaseTokenizer` does not), and no overlapping open PR exists. The alternatives the PR lists (move it into ChatProcessor or BaseTokenizer) are correctly rejected.
- HF transformers passes the whole `special_tokens_map` (bos, eos, unk, pad, ...) into the template. This PR covers only bos/eos. That is fine as a minimal fix, since no in-repo template is known to need the others.
- Prompt/response boundary: with the asset template, `apply_chat_template([user], add_generation_prompt=True)` renders `<bos>user\nQ<eos>assistant\n`, which is still a token prefix of the full sequence. So `_require_token_prefix` keeps working, and the supervised suffix is `answer + [EOS]`, as asserted by `TestHFBackendTokenizerChatLabels`.
- Pre-existing, out of scope: when `bos_token == eos_token`, the base tokenizer sets only `bos_token`, so `{{ eos_token }}` still renders `""` on the default path. `HFBackendTokenizer.__init__` repairs this only for the experiment.
</details>

Not verified: I didn't check SFT loss on a real Llama 3 tokenizer. The asset-based reasoning above is from reading the code.

These two overrides (this one and the BOS check in `encode` at 460-463) are copied line for line from `HFBackendTokenizer.apply_chat_template` / `HFBackendTokenizer.encode` in `torchtitan/experiments/transformers_modeling_backend/tokenizer.py:46-55`. Leaving them in the subclass means the same logic lives in two places, and every call runs the `setdefault` and `startswith` checks twice.

Please delete both methods from `HFBackendTokenizer` in this PR. Its `__init__` eos repair and the `{% generation %}` rewrite in `set_chat_template` can stay. Also update its class docstring ("The base tokenizer only passes messages. This subclass auto-injects special tokens..."), which is no longer true. That is roughly -10 LoC.

nodes.body:
This overrides an explicit `add_bos=True` from the caller, so `add_bos` no longer means what the `encode` docstring above says ("Whether to add BOS token"). It now means "make sure the text starts with BOS". That is a reasonable contract, and it also stops pretraining text that starts with the literal BOS string from getting two BOS ids (`text_datasets.py:53`). But the docstring should say it, since `encode` is shared by every `HuggingFaceTokenizer` caller.

Smallest fix: document it in the `add_bos` arg docstring, e.g. `add_bos (bool): Whether to add a BOS token. Skipped if text already starts with bos_token.` The other option is to make the decision at the two `ChatProcessor` call sites (`text_datasets.py:166,179`) with `add_bos=not text.startswith(bos_token)`. That keeps `encode` literal, but it needs `bos_token` on `BaseTokenizer`, so I'd go with the docstring.

## Alternatives considered

- Point every recipe at `HFBackendTokenizer`. That subclass also rewrites `{% generation %}` tags and repairs eos when bos and eos are the same string. Default SFT should not depend on the experiment tokenizer for variables the base tokenizer already knows.
- Leave the two overrides on `HFBackendTokenizer`. No. After the base change they only ran the same `setdefault` and prefix check a second time.
- Inject the strings in `BaseTokenizer.apply_chat_template`. The base class has no `bos_token` or `eos_token`.
- Splice BOS/EOS inside `ChatProcessor` after rendering. The template already says where they go, and any other `apply_chat_template` caller would still drop them.

## User-facing changes

This changes SFT chat strings for every recipe that uses `HuggingFaceTokenizer` and a template that references `bos_token` / `eos_token`. Templates that do not reference those names are unchanged, because the extra kwargs are unused. `encode` changes only when the text already starts with `bos_token`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `{{ bos_token }}` / `{{ eos_token }}` render as empty strings | They render this tokenizer's BOS and EOS strings (`""` if unset) |
| `encode(rendered, add_bos=True)` prepends BOS even when the template already wrote it | One BOS id |
| EOS shows up only if the caller appends it (ChatProcessor appends one at the end) | EOS is present wherever the template writes `{{ eos_token }}`, including between turns |
| Caller-supplied `bos_token=` / `eos_token=` | Still win |

## Numerics

Not bitwise-identical. Chat token ids change for those templates, so SFT loss on the same rows will not match the base commit `4759738106a6f198a4dd41c78d2a754be5d0b2c4`. No GPU loss comparison. No golden loss files to regenerate: this does not change the model forward, only the chat strings fed to it. Pretraining text that does not start with `bos_token` encodes as before.

## Testing

- The token behavior is the previous commit on this branch. This commit does not change `setdefault` or the prefix check. `py_compile` of the four touched files succeeded. `ufmt` 2.3.0 reported them already formatted.
- `/opt/homebrew/anaconda3/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_chat_dataset.py -q` still does not collect here (`spmd_types` has no `rules`, then NumPy 2.2.6 vs bottleneck). CI has to run it. `{% generation %}` coverage stays in `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/test_tokenizer.py`.

## Known issues / follow-ups

Local collection failure above is an environment mismatch, not this diff. No follow-up code change.

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The bug is real on `main`: Llama-3-style templates that reference `bos_token`/`eos_token` render without them on the default SFT path. The fix belongs in `HuggingFaceTokenizer`, but it should replace the identical experiment overrides rather than duplicate them. This touches core, so a maintainer still needs to review.

**What this PR does.** It moves two behaviors from the experiment `HFBackendTokenizer` into `HuggingFaceTokenizer`:
- `apply_chat_template` passes `bos_token`/`eos_token` to the Jinja template (caller kwargs still win).
- `encode` skips prepending BOS when the text already starts with the BOS string.

SFT token ids change for templates that reference those variables. That is expected and explained in the description. No golden loss files are affected.

**Example.** Test asset template `{{ bos_token }}{% for m in messages %}{{ m.role }}\n{{ m.content }}{{ eos_token }}{% endfor %}`, messages user/hi, assistant/yo, run through `ChatProcessor`:
```text
main: "user\nhiassistant\nyo"                                   -> [BOS] user\nhi assistant\nyo [EOS appended by ChatProcessor]
PR:   "<|begin_of_text|>user\nhi<|end_of_text|>assistant\nyo<|end_of_text|>" -> [BOS] user\nhi [EOS] assistant\nyo [EOS]
```
The real Llama 3 template writes `{{- bos_token }}` and `<|eot_id|>`. So on `main` only BOS was missing; ChatProcessor's `add_bos=True` was covering for it.

### Must fix
1. The PR description's "Summary (human-written)" section is empty. The author needs to fill it in.
2. `torchtitan/experiments/transformers_modeling_backend/tokenizer.py:46-55`: `HFBackendTokenizer.apply_chat_template` and `.encode` are now exact duplicates of the new base code. Delete them and fix the class docstring (details inline at `tokenizer.py:429`).
3. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_chat_dataset.py:344`: `TestHuggingFaceTokenizerChatTemplateTokens` duplicates `test_shifted_by_one`. Delete it, and switch `TestHFBackendTokenizerChatLabels` to `HuggingFaceTokenizer`.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/components/tokenizer.py:460`: `encode` now overrides an explicit `add_bos=True`. Document that in the `add_bos` docstring.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_chat_dataset.py:200`: four of the five new token assertions are implied by the exact-string check or by the code just above them.
- `torchtitan/components/renderer.py:80-81`: the `DefaultRenderer` error message still names `bos_token` as a missing template variable. Change the example (e.g. "`pad_token`, `unk_token`, ...") or say "HF's full `special_tokens_map`".

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Gate: the problem is concrete (asset template plus Llama 3), the root cause is in the right layer (the tokenizer owns `bos_token`/`eos_token`; `BaseTokenizer` does not), and no overlapping open PR exists. The alternatives the PR lists (move it into ChatProcessor or BaseTokenizer) are correctly rejected.
- HF transformers passes the whole `special_tokens_map` (bos, eos, unk, pad, ...) into the template. This PR covers only bos/eos. That is fine as a minimal fix, since no in-repo template is known to need the others.
- Prompt/response boundary: with the asset template, `apply_chat_template([user], add_generation_prompt=True)` renders `<bos>user\nQ<eos>assistant\n`, which is still a token prefix of the full sequence. So `_require_token_prefix` keeps working, and the supervised suffix is `answer + [EOS]`, as asserted by `TestHFBackendTokenizerChatLabels`.
- Pre-existing, out of scope: when `bos_token == eos_token`, the base tokenizer sets only `bos_token`, so `{{ eos_token }}` still renders `""` on the default path. `HFBackendTokenizer.__init__` repairs this only for the experiment.
</details>

Not verified: I didn't check SFT loss on a real Llama 3 tokenizer. The asset-based reasoning above is from reading the code.
